elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to an Affiliate.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 expressly permits PB to assign, sublicense, or transfer the Agreement and all rights and obligations to any Affiliate without SFJ's consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with a merger.
elements.evidence: PB may transfer the Agreement to a successor in connection with a transfer of the relevant business or assets, expressly including a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The successor exception covers a sale or other transfer, including a sale of stock, which encompasses an acquisition transaction.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: PB may transfer the Agreement to a successor in connection with a sale or transfer of all or substantially all of the business or assets to which the Agreement relates.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement or any of its rights or duties without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Although the general rule requires PB's consent, the surviving notwithstanding clause permits SFJ to assign its Approval Payment rights to limited partners or a liquidating trust without PB's consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence states that the other Party's required consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement or any of its rights or duties to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The added final sentence provides that in no event may SFJ sell, assign, sublicense, or otherwise transfer the Agreement or any rights or duties to a competitor of PB.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right triggered by Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.6 now expressly states that SFJ may not terminate the Agreement following the specified Change of Control of PB. The retained payment language does not independently grant a termination right.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: PB has a consent-free right to transfer the Agreement to a successor in connection with the specified merger, stock-sale, asset-sale, or other transfer transactions.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 imposes no written-notice condition on PB's successor assignment. Section 14.2.6 only requires notice of a Change of Control and does not demonstrably cover every successor assignment, including all qualifying asset transfers.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: The consent-free Affiliate/successor exception was limited to PB. SFJ's assignment of the entire Agreement to a successor remains subject to PB's consent under the general rule.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No operative provision requires SFJ to provide written notice of a successor assignment.

elements.element: Customer's assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: PB may assign to any Affiliate without SFJ's consent, even where that Affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to Customer's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For PB assignments subject to the general consent requirement, the clause states that SFJ's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor's assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The notwithstanding clause allows SFJ to assign Approval Payment rights to limited partners or a liquidating trust without PB's consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For SFJ assignments subject to the general consent requirement, the clause states that PB's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The redline achieves the principal Customer assignment rights, competitor prohibition, consent standard, and elimination of SFJ's change-of-control termination right. It does not fully satisfy the preferred position because SFJ retains consent-free rights to assign Approval Payment rights. It also fails the fallback because successor-assignment notice is incomplete, SFJ lacks a consent-free successor right, and both sides retain consent-free non-successor exceptions. The drafting also leaves an obsolete termination-payment consequence immediately after prohibiting the termination, reducing clarity. Because neither complete level is reached, the redline is not minimal under the stated standard, although unrelated commercial terms are generally preserved.
